items.title: Al Gafa interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 2, 2023
items.q: There’s a very humorous story in Bill Crow’s book of Jazz Anecdotes

ctx.x: Well I thought he was a genius. I mean when he played, yeah, he was definitely something not of this earth. He was in another planet when he was doing these things. He played, he was innovative and he was quick and humorous, and if he wanted me to play a chord he would play it in his solo. And if I’m listening I’m hearing it easy. It makes it easy for me. And he heard everything I played. I don’t know how he did that but I’ll give you an example. One night I changed a chord in an original composition, I changed…

There’s a very humorous story in Bill Crow’s book of Jazz Anecdotes about Dizzy doing a Latin number and the bass player was just supposed to play one note on a particular beat and he lost it and etcetera, it’s a fairly long story, but I wondered if playing Dizzy’s Latin repertoire was something new for you and was it an adjustment?

It was not new and let me tell you we were playing a bunch of my tunes also. So yeah, there was no — you know Dizzy had arrangements on let’s say like “One Note Samba.” He had his arrangement of “One Note Samba.” I didn’t play my arrangement of “One Note Samba,” we played his arrangement. So everything was, it was not new and you tried to be as creative as you can every night. You know you can’t always do that but you
